title: Portrait Cut for Two Speakers
tests: Tests speaker-aware portrait reframing of a two-person conversation without losing either speaking turn.

faults.what: The crop does not follow the requested speakers: the light-blue-shirted man is cut off at the left edge, while the framing primarily favors the bearded man.
The woman's face is absent from every supplied output frame; only a sliver of her hair or shoulder appears at the right edge, so her answer is not presented as requested.

judge.summary: The output is a caption-free portrait crop, but it frames the wrong area and fails to show both requested speakers clearly.

must_haves.item: The output is a 9:16 portrait edit of the attached office conversation.
must_haves.why: The output frames have approximately 9:16 portrait proportions and show the same office scene and people.

must_haves.item: The man is centred and his face is fully visible during his question.
must_haves.why: The light-blue-shirted man is clipped by the left edge in all supplied output frames rather than being centred with his whole face visible.

must_haves.item: The woman is centred and her face is fully visible during her answer.
must_haves.why: The woman is almost entirely outside the crop throughout the supplied samples, with no visible face.

must_haves.item: Both speaking turns remain in their original order, with the full 10 seconds and original audio in sync.
must_haves.why: The reported 10.1-second duration retains approximately the requested length, but the audio report contains no clear speech, and neither original-audio preservation nor speaking-turn order and synchronization can be verified from these samples.

must_haves.item: The image is not stretched and contains no added captions.
must_haves.why: People and office features appear proportionate, and no captions are visible.
